claim: ESCRT-III subunits polymerize rapidly on yeast endosomes.
source: By quantitative fluorescence lattice light-sheet microscopy, we have shown that ESCRT-III subunits polymerize rapidly on yeast endosomes, together with the recruitment of at least two Vps4 hexamers.
evidence: Supported by LLSM imaging data showing rapid appearance of ESCRT-III fluorescence signals on endosomes

claim: At least two Vps4 hexamers are recruited together with ESCRT-III polymerization on yeast endosomes.
source: By quantitative fluorescence lattice light-sheet microscopy, we have shown that ESCRT-III subunits polymerize rapidly on yeast endosomes, together with the recruitment of at least two Vps4 hexamers.
evidence: Supported by quantitative LLSM measurements of Vps4 molecules

claim: ESCRT-III assemblies have lifetimes of 3–45 seconds.
source: During their 3–45 s lifetimes, the ESCRT-III assemblies accumulated 75–200 Snf7 and 15–50 Vps24 molecules.
evidence: Supported by time-resolved LLSM tracking data

claim: ESCRT-III assemblies accumulate 75–200 Snf7 molecules during their lifetime.
source: During their 3–45 s lifetimes, the ESCRT-III assemblies accumulated 75–200 Snf7 and 15–50 Vps24 molecules.
evidence: Supported by quantitative fluorescence intensity measurements calibrated to single molecule detection

claim: ESCRT-III assemblies accumulate 15–50 Vps24 molecules during their lifetime.
source: During their 3–45 s lifetimes, the ESCRT-III assemblies accumulated 75–200 Snf7 and 15–50 Vps24 molecules.
evidence: Supported by quantitative fluorescence intensity measurements calibrated to single molecule detection

claim: Productive budding events require at least two additional Vps4 hexamers beyond the initial recruitment.
source: Productive budding events required at least two additional Vps4 hexamers.
evidence: Supported by comparison of Vps4 accumulation in productive vs non-productive events

claim: Membrane budding is associated with continuous, stochastic exchange of Vps4 and ESCRT-III components.
source: Membrane budding was associated with continuous, stochastic exchange of Vps4 and ESCRT-III components, rather than steady growth of fixed assemblies, and depended on Vps4 ATPase activity.
evidence: Supported by time-resolved fluorescence intensity fluctuations during budding events

claim: Membrane budding does not involve steady growth of fixed assemblies.
source: Membrane budding was associated with continuous, stochastic exchange of Vps4 and ESCRT-III components, rather than steady growth of fixed assemblies, and depended on Vps4 ATPase activity.
evidence: Supported by observation of fluctuating rather than monotonically increasing fluorescence signals

claim: Membrane budding depends on Vps4 ATPase activity.
source: Membrane budding was associated with continuous, stochastic exchange of Vps4 and ESCRT-III components, rather than steady growth of fixed assemblies, and depended on Vps4 ATPase activity.
evidence: Supported by experiments with Vps4E233Q ATPase-deficient mutant

claim: An all-or-none step leads to final release of ESCRT-III and Vps4.
source: An all-or-none step led to final release of ESCRT-III and Vps4.
evidence: Supported by observation of abrupt termination of fluorescence signals

claim: Acute disruption of Vps4 recruitment stalls membrane budding.
source: Tomographic electron microscopy demonstrated that acute disruption of Vps4 recruitment stalled membrane budding.
evidence: Supported by electron tomography of cells after rapamycin-induced Vps4 depletion

claim: Multiple Vps4 hexamers (four or more) draw together several ESCRT-III filaments.
source: We propose a model in which multiple Vps4 hexamers (four or more) draw together several ESCRT-III filaments.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental observations

claim: Vps4 hexamer activity induces cargo crowding and inward membrane buckling.
source: This process induces cargo crowding and inward membrane buckling, followed by constriction of the nascent bud neck and ultimately ILV generation by vesicle fission.
evidence: This is part of the proposed mechanistic model

claim: The ESCRT machinery mediates reverse membrane scission.
source: The ESCRT (endosomal sorting complexes required for transport) machinery mediates 'reverse' membrane budding in distinct but topologically related processes, including formation of intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) in multivesicular bodies (MVBs), plasma-membrane repair and microvesicle formation, abscission in cytokinesis, budding of certain viruses, and nuclear membrane resealing (Christ et al., 2017) as well as membrane deformation towards the cytosol (McCullough et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature

claim: MVB formation depends on ESCRT-0, ESCRT-I and ESCRT-II hetero-multimers.
source: MVB formation depends on the hetero-multimers ESCRT-0, ESCRT-I and ESCRT-II, which capture ubiquitinated cargo on the endosomal limiting membrane (Bilodeau et al., 2002; Katzmann et al., 2001; Alam et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: ESCRT-0, ESCRT-I and ESCRT-II capture ubiquitinated cargo on the endosomal limiting membrane.
source: MVB formation depends on the hetero-multimers ESCRT-0, ESCRT-I and ESCRT-II, which capture ubiquitinated cargo on the endosomal limiting membrane (Bilodeau et al., 2002; Katzmann et al., 2001; Alam et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Budding requires recruitment of ESCRT-III heteropolymers and Vps4.
source: Budding then requires recruitment of ESCRT-III heteropolymers and the type I AAA+ (ATPase associated with a variety of cellular activities) ATPase, Vps4 (Babst et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: In yeast cells, ESCRT-III includes Snf7 as a major structural component.
source: In yeast cells, ESCRT-III includes a major structural component, Snf7, core subunits Vps2, Vps20, and Vps24, and accessory proteins Did2, Vps60 and Ist1 (McCullough et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: ESCRT-III core subunits include Vps2, Vps20, and Vps24.
source: In yeast cells, ESCRT-III includes a major structural component, Snf7, core subunits Vps2, Vps20, and Vps24, and accessory proteins Did2, Vps60 and Ist1 (McCullough et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: ESCRT-III accessory proteins include Did2, Vps60 and Ist1.
source: In yeast cells, ESCRT-III includes a major structural component, Snf7, core subunits Vps2, Vps20, and Vps24, and accessory proteins Did2, Vps60 and Ist1 (McCullough et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: Interaction of Vps20 with ESCRT-II triggers membrane recruitment of Snf7.
source: Interaction of Vps20 with ESCRT-II triggers membrane recruitment of Snf7, which in turn recruits Vps24 and Vps2.
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Snf7 recruits Vps24 and Vps2.
source: Interaction of Vps20 with ESCRT-II triggers membrane recruitment of Snf7, which in turn recruits Vps24 and Vps2.
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Vps2 recruits Vps4 to ESCRT-III filaments.
source: Vps2 recruits Vps4 to these filaments and together with Vps24 may also restrict Snf7 polymerization (Babst et al., 2002; Teis et al., 2008; Saksena et al., 2009; Teis et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Vps2 and Vps24 may restrict Snf7 polymerization.
source: Vps2 recruits Vps4 to these filaments and together with Vps24 may also restrict Snf7 polymerization (Babst et al., 2002; Teis et al., 2008; Saksena et al., 2009; Teis et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research, with 'may' indicating some uncertainty

claim: In vitro, Snf7 alone or together with Vps2 and Vps24 forms curved filaments.
source: In vitro, Snf7 alone or together with Vps2 and Vps24, forms curved filaments (Henne et al., 2012; Mierzwa et al., 2017; Schöneberg et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published in vitro studies

claim: In cells, Vps4 forms a hexameric ring when recruited to ESCRT-III filaments.
source: In cells, Vps4 forms a hexameric ring when recruited to ESCRT-III filaments (Caillat et al., 2015; Monroe et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: A Vps4 hexamer can unfold individual ESCRT-III subunits by ATP-dependent translocation through its central pore.
source: A Vps4 hexamer can unfold individual ESCRT-III subunits by ATP-dependent translocation through its central pore (Scott et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2015; Monroe et al., 2017; Su et al., 2017); in vitro, this process promotes disassembly of ESCRT-III polymers (Davies et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: In vitro, Vps4-mediated unfolding of ESCRT-III subunits promotes disassembly of ESCRT-III polymers.
source: A Vps4 hexamer can unfold individual ESCRT-III subunits by ATP-dependent translocation through its central pore (Scott et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2015; Monroe et al., 2017; Su et al., 2017); in vitro, this process promotes disassembly of ESCRT-III polymers (Davies et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published in vitro studies

claim: The N-terminus of Vps4 contains a MIT domain.
source: The N-terminus of Vps4 contains a 'Microtubule Interacting and Trafficking' (MIT) domain, which interacts with C-terminal 'MIT interaction motifs' (MIM) on ESCRT-III subunits (Obita et al., 2007; Stuchell-Brereton et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to published structural studies

claim: The MIT domain of Vps4 interacts with C-terminal MIM motifs on ESCRT-III subunits.
source: The N-terminus of Vps4 contains a 'Microtubule Interacting and Trafficking' (MIT) domain, which interacts with C-terminal 'MIT interaction motifs' (MIM) on ESCRT-III subunits (Obita et al., 2007; Stuchell-Brereton et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to published structural studies

claim: Binding of MIT domains to MIM motifs releases Vps4 auto-inhibition.
source: Binding of MIT domains to these motifs, exposed in the assembled polymer (Obita et al., 2007; Stuchell-Brereton et al., 2007), releases Vps4 auto-inhibition (Merrill and Hanson, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Formation of ILVs requires coordinated interaction of Vps4 with MIMs of Vps2 and Snf7.
source: Formation of ILVs requires coordinated interaction of Vps4 with MIMs of Vps2 and Snf7 (Adell et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: ESCRT-III filaments can deform membranes in vivo.
source: Since ESCRT-III filaments can deform membranes in vivo (Hanson et al., 2008) and in vitro (Wollert et al., 2009; Wollert and Hurley, 2010; Schöneberg et al., 2017), it has been suggested that their assembly and/or disassembly provides the driving force for budding (Fabrikant et al., 2009; Chiaruttini et al., 2015; Wollert and Hurley, 2010; Adell et al., 2014; Wemmer et al., 2011; Mageswaran et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: ESCRT-III filaments can deform membranes in vitro.
source: Since ESCRT-III filaments can deform membranes in vivo (Hanson et al., 2008) and in vitro (Wollert et al., 2009; Wollert and Hurley, 2010; Schöneberg et al., 2017), it has been suggested that their assembly and/or disassembly provides the driving force for budding (Fabrikant et al., 2009; Chiaruttini et al., 2015; Wollert and Hurley, 2010; Adell et al., 2014; Wemmer et al., 2011; Mageswaran et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published in vitro studies

claim: It has been suggested that ESCRT-III assembly and/or disassembly provides the driving force for budding.
source: Since ESCRT-III filaments can deform membranes in vivo (Hanson et al., 2008) and in vitro (Wollert et al., 2009; Wollert and Hurley, 2010; Schöneberg et al., 2017), it has been suggested that their assembly and/or disassembly provides the driving force for budding (Fabrikant et al., 2009; Chiaruttini et al., 2015; Wollert and Hurley, 2010; Adell et al., 2014; Wemmer et al., 2011; Mageswaran et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a summary of existing models in the literature

claim: Live cell imaging of mammalian cells overexpressing fluorescently tagged ESCRT-III and Vps4 showed that ESCRT-III arrived before Vps4 at sites of HIV budding.
source: Live cell imaging of mammalian cells overexpressing fluorescently tagged ESCRT-III and Vps4 showed that ESCRT-III arrived before Vps4 at the sites of HIV budding, during plasma membrane repair and at the nuclear membrane (Bleck et al., 2014; Baumgärtel et al., 2011; Prescher et al., 2015; Jouvenet et al., 2011; Guizetti et al., 2011; Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2015; Jimenez et al., 2014; Raab et al., 2016; Denais et al., 2016; Mierzwa et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published live cell imaging studies

claim: Live cell imaging showed ESCRT-III arrived before Vps4 during plasma membrane repair.
source: Live cell imaging of mammalian cells overexpressing fluorescently tagged ESCRT-III and Vps4 showed that ESCRT-III arrived before Vps4 at the sites of HIV budding, during plasma membrane repair and at the nuclear membrane (Bleck et al., 2014; Baumgärtel et al., 2011; Prescher et al., 2015; Jouvenet et al., 2011; Guizetti et al., 2011; Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2015; Jimenez et al., 2014; Raab et al., 2016; Denais et al., 2016; Mierzwa et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published live cell imaging studies

claim: Live cell imaging showed ESCRT-III arrived before Vps4 at the nuclear membrane.
source: Live cell imaging of mammalian cells overexpressing fluorescently tagged ESCRT-III and Vps4 showed that ESCRT-III arrived before Vps4 at the sites of HIV budding, during plasma membrane repair and at the nuclear membrane (Bleck et al., 2014; Baumgärtel et al., 2011; Prescher et al., 2015; Jouvenet et al., 2011; Guizetti et al., 2011; Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2015; Jimenez et al., 2014; Raab et al., 2016; Denais et al., 2016; Mierzwa et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published live cell imaging studies

claim: ESCRT-III and Vps4 are recruited to the midbody prior to abscission.
source: ESCRT-III and Vps4 are recruited to the midbody prior to abscission, but whether the recruitment is correlated remains to be determined (Elia et al., 2011; Mierzwa et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Whether ESCRT-III and Vps4 recruitment to the midbody is correlated remains to be determined.
source: ESCRT-III and Vps4 are recruited to the midbody prior to abscission, but whether the recruitment is correlated remains to be determined (Elia et al., 2011; Mierzwa et al., 2017).
evidence: This acknowledges a gap in knowledge based on cited literature

claim: Previous live cell imaging experiments did not achieve the required levels of sensitivity, or spatial and temporal resolution to trace the inherently rapid dynamics of ESCRT.
source: These experiments did not achieve the required levels of sensitivity, or spatial and temporal resolution to trace the inherently rapid dynamics.
evidence: This is an assessment of prior work based on technical limitations

claim: A large fraction (60%) of ESCRT recruitment traces did not exceed 62 Snf7-eGFP molecules.
source: During their 3–45 s lifetimes, recruitment of these proteins appeared to be stochastic, but mutually correlated; a large fraction (60%) of the traces did not exceed 62, 33 and 48 molecules (8 hexamers) of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP, respectively.
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of LLSM data

claim: A large fraction (60%) of ESCRT recruitment traces did not exceed 33 Vps24-eGFP molecules.
source: During their 3–45 s lifetimes, recruitment of these proteins appeared to be stochastic, but mutually correlated; a large fraction (60%) of the traces did not exceed 62, 33 and 48 molecules (8 hexamers) of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP, respectively.
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of LLSM data

claim: A large fraction (60%) of ESCRT recruitment traces did not exceed 48 Vps4-eGFP molecules (8 hexamers).
source: During their 3–45 s lifetimes, recruitment of these proteins appeared to be stochastic, but mutually correlated; a large fraction (60%) of the traces did not exceed 62, 33 and 48 molecules (8 hexamers) of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP, respectively.
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of LLSM data

claim: Non-productive events on average recruited only 12 Vps4 molecules (2 hexamers).
source: Although non-productive events displayed similar recruitment dynamics, on average they only recruited 12 Vps4 molecules (2 hexamers).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of LLSM data comparing productive and non-productive events

claim: Vps4 is not needed to sustain ESCRT-III dynamics.
source: Vps4 was not needed to sustain ESCRT-III dynamics, but electron tomography showed that it was essential for ILV budding and scission.
evidence: Supported by LLSM data showing ESCRT-III dynamics persist in Vps4E233Q mutant

claim: Electron tomography showed that Vps4 is essential for ILV budding and scission.
source: Vps4 was not needed to sustain ESCRT-III dynamics, but electron tomography showed that it was essential for ILV budding and scission.
evidence: Supported by electron tomography data after Vps4 depletion

claim: Direct fusion of eGFP to the C-terminus of ESCRT-III subunits interferes with function.
source: Direct fusion of eGFP to the C-terminus of ESCRT-III subunits interferes with function (Teis et al., 2008), probably because of incompatibility with the periodicity of ESCRT-III polymers (Tang et al., 2015) (Shen et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research and structural considerations

claim: A 70-residue LAP linker was inserted between the C-terminus of Snf7 or Vps24 and the N-terminus of eGFP.
source: We therefore inserted the 70-residue localization and affinity purification (LAP) linker between the C-terminus of Snf7 or Vps24 and the N-terminus of eGFP (Guizetti et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the experimental design used in the study

claim: The expression levels of Snf7-LAP-eGFP and Vps24-LAP-eGFP fusion proteins were comparable to the untagged proteins.
source: The expression levels of the fusion proteins were comparable to the untagged proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in the figure

claim: Direct fusion of eGFP to the C-terminus of Vps4 affects function.
source: Direct fusion of eGFP to the C-terminus of Vps4 likewise affects function, because of the positions of the C-terminal helix in higher-order Vps4 assemblies (Scott et al., 2005) (Landsberg et al., 2009; Caillat et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural studies

claim: A 3xHA linker was added to the C-terminus of Vps4 before eGFP or mCherry.
source: We added a 3xHA linker and integrated 3xHA-eGFP or 3xHA-mCherry at the C-terminus of endogenous Vps4 by homologous recombination.
evidence: This describes the experimental design

claim: Vps4-3xHA-eGFP was expressed as a full-length fusion protein at endogenous levels.
source: Subcellular fractionation showed that Vps4-3xHA-eGFP (Vps4-eGFP) was expressed as a full-length fusion protein at endogenous levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b,c).
evidence: Supported by subcellular fractionation and western blot data

claim: Expression of Snf7-eGFP alone blocked MVB sorting to the vacuole.
source: Live-cell, wide-field fluorescence microscopy showed that expression of Snf7-eGFP alone blocked MVB sorting to the vacuole (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), but not when it was co-expressed with endogenous Snf7 (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by live cell microscopy data

claim: Co-expression of Snf7-eGFP with endogenous Snf7 did not block MVB sorting to the vacuole.
source: Live-cell, wide-field fluorescence microscopy showed that expression of Snf7-eGFP alone blocked MVB sorting to the vacuole (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), but not when it was co-expressed with endogenous Snf7 (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by live cell microscopy data

claim: Snf7-eGFP protomers need to be interspaced with at least 2 untagged Snf7 molecules to avoid steric clashes within the polymer.
source: Inspection of the structure of Snf7-polymers (Tang et al., 2015; Shen et al., 2014) suggests that Snf7-eGFP protomers need to be interspaced with at least 2 untagged Snf7 molecules to avoid steric clashes within the polymer.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural data from cited literature

claim: Vps24-eGFP could fully replace the corresponding untagged protein without compromising trafficking of mCherry-Cps1 or Mup1-mCherry.
source: Vps24-eGFP, Vps4-eGFP and Vps4-mCherry could, however, fully replace the corresponding untagged proteins without compromising trafficking of mCherry-Cps1 or Mup1-mCherry (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Supported by live cell microscopy showing proper cargo trafficking

claim: Vps4-eGFP could fully replace the corresponding untagged protein without compromising trafficking of mCherry-Cps1 or Mup1-mCherry.
source: Vps24-eGFP, Vps4-eGFP and Vps4-mCherry could, however, fully replace the corresponding untagged proteins without compromising trafficking of mCherry-Cps1 or Mup1-mCherry (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Supported by live cell microscopy showing proper cargo trafficking

claim: Vps4-mCherry could fully replace the corresponding untagged protein without compromising trafficking of mCherry-Cps1 or Mup1-mCherry.
source: Vps24-eGFP, Vps4-eGFP and Vps4-mCherry could, however, fully replace the corresponding untagged proteins without compromising trafficking of mCherry-Cps1 or Mup1-mCherry (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Supported by live cell microscopy showing proper cargo trafficking

claim: Wild-type cells expressing Snf7-eGFP along with untagged Snf7 could grow on canavanine.
source: Moreover, wild-type cells expressing Snf7-eGFP along with untagged Snf7 could grow on canavanine, as could cells expressing Vps24-eGFP, Vps4-eGFP as expected for a fully functional MVB pathway (Lin et al., 2008), while the deletion mutants of any of these three proteins could not (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Supported by canavanine sensitivity assay data

claim: Cells expressing Vps24-eGFP could grow on canavanine.
source: Moreover, wild-type cells expressing Snf7-eGFP along with untagged Snf7 could grow on canavanine, as could cells expressing Vps24-eGFP, Vps4-eGFP as expected for a fully functional MVB pathway (Lin et al., 2008), while the deletion mutants of any of these three proteins could not (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Supported by canavanine sensitivity assay data

claim: Cells expressing Vps4-eGFP could grow on canavanine.
source: Moreover, wild-type cells expressing Snf7-eGFP along with untagged Snf7 could grow on canavanine, as could cells expressing Vps24-eGFP, Vps4-eGFP as expected for a fully functional MVB pathway (Lin et al., 2008), while the deletion mutants of any of these three proteins could not (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Supported by canavanine sensitivity assay data

claim: Deletion mutants of Snf7, Vps24, or Vps4 could not grow on canavanine.
source: Moreover, wild-type cells expressing Snf7-eGFP along with untagged Snf7 could grow on canavanine, as could cells expressing Vps24-eGFP, Vps4-eGFP as expected for a fully functional MVB pathway (Lin et al., 2008), while the deletion mutants of any of these three proteins could not (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Supported by canavanine sensitivity assay data

claim: The ratio of Snf7 to Vps24 is about 3–6 in the membrane-bound fraction of wild-type cells.
source: Previous work has shown a ratio of Snf7 to Vps24 of about 3–6 in the membrane-bound fraction of wild-type cells (Teis et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to published biochemical data

claim: The mean ratio of Snf7-eGFP to Vps24-eGFP measured by calibrated fluorescence intensity is about 1.4:1.
source: The mean ratio of Snf7-eGFP to Vps24-eGFP measured by calibrated fluorescence intensity in the events studied here is about 1.4:1.
evidence: Supported by quantitative fluorescence measurements in this study

claim: To estimate the number of total Snf7 molecules in any event, the number of eGFP molecules was multiplied by a factor of 3.
source: In the text below, to estimate the number of total Snf7 molecules in any event, we have therefore multiplied by a factor of 3 the number of eGFP molecules determined directly from the intensity data.
evidence: This describes the calculation method used to account for unlabeled Snf7

claim: 187 Vps4-fluorophore puncta were detected in 1390 sectioned cells, corresponding to approximately two per cell.
source: We detected 187 Vps4-fluorophore puncta in 1390 sectioned cells, corresponding to approximately two per cell (0.14 fluorescent spots/cell/300 nm-thick section or 1–3 spots/5 μm cell).

claim: In living cells, 5–10 Vps4 puncta per cell were detected.
source: In living cells, we detected 5–10 Vps4 puncta/cell, indicating loss of signal during the freeze-substitution procedure.

claim: Tomographic analysis was carried out on thick sections from 31 cells with 38 Vps4-fluorescent puncta.
source: We carried out tomographic analysis on thick sections from 31 cells with 38 Vps4-fluorescent puncta and of four unlabeled cells and found that the 38 puncta correlated with 36 areas with one to three MVBs (a total of 83 MVBs altogether, Supplementary file 1).

claim: 38 Vps4-fluorescent puncta correlated with 36 areas containing one to three MVBs (83 MVBs total).
source: We carried out tomographic analysis on thick sections from 31 cells with 38 Vps4-fluorescent puncta and of four unlabeled cells and found that the 38 puncta correlated with 36 areas with one to three MVBs (a total of 83 MVBs altogether, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by correlative light and electron microscopy data

claim: Most of the MVBs (89%) were associated with vacuoles.

claim: MVBs contained on average 21 and up to about 65 ILVs of uniform size.

source: Within the full volumes of living yeast cells (Figure 3a), we tracked the 3D positions of ESCRT-III and Vps4-containing objects (a total of 5,000–12,000 diffraction-limited objects), with 850 – 960 ms time resolution and three eGFP-molecule sensitivity (data for Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP are summarized in Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the detection sensitivity of the LLSM method

claim: Two classes of fluorescent signals were detected: class I with diffraction-limited objects distributed throughout the cytosol, and class II with a mixture of diffraction-limited and non-diffraction limited fluorescent objects of relatively high intensity and low mobility located close to the vacuole.
source: In WT cells expressing Snf7-eGFP together with endogenous Snf7, Vps24-eGFP or Vps4-eGFP (Videos 2–4), we detected two classes of fluorescent signals: class I, with diffraction-limited objects distributed throughout the cytosol, and class II, with a mixture of diffraction-limited and non-diffraction limited fluorescent objects, both of relatively high intensity and low mobility, located close to the vacuole (Figure 3b).
evidence: Supported by LLSM imaging data

claim: A typical cell contained 5–10 mobile, diffraction-limited puncta.
source: Typically, a cell contained 5–10 mobile, diffraction-limited puncta (i.e., < 300 × 300 x 600 nm), each relatively weak.
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of LLSM data

claim: The size of diffraction-limited puncta is compatible with the sizes of individual MVBs in yeast (<250 nm).
source: The size is compatible with the sizes of individual MVBs in yeast (<250 nm).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of optical and EM measurements

claim: When co-expressed, Snf7-eGFP and Vps24-eGFP colocalized with Vps4-mCherry.
source: When co-expressed, Snf7-eGFP and Vps24-eGFP colocalized with Vps4-mCherry (Figure 3c,d).
evidence: Supported by dual-color LLSM imaging data

claim: The larger class II objects are pairs or small clusters of perivacuolar MVBs.
source: Correlative electron microscopy, described above, revealed that the larger class II objects are pairs or small clusters of perivacuolar MVBs (Figure 2e).
evidence: Supported by correlative light and electron microscopy

claim: Cargo reached perivacuolar MVBs 5–10 min after the onset of endocytosis.
source: LLSM 3D visualization showed that cargo reached them 5–10 min after the onset of endocytosis (Video 8, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse LLSM imaging of cargo trafficking

claim: A common feature of all traces was an abrupt increase from baseline in the fluorescence intensity for ESCRT-III subunits Snf7 or Vps24, to levels of about 60 and 14 subunits, respectively.
source: A common feature of all traces was an abrupt increase from baseline in the fluorescence intensity for ESCRT-III subunits Snf7 or Vps24, to levels of about 60 and 14 subunits, respectively.
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of fluorescence traces

claim: In most cases, the intensity fluctuated with no detectable pattern and no net accumulation until an abrupt decline to baseline after a variable time interval.
source: In most cases, the intensity then fluctuated with no detectable pattern and no net accumulation until an abrupt decline to baseline after a variable time interval (Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: Supported by analysis of fluorescence intensity time traces

claim: Only in about 32% of Snf7-eGFP or Vps24-eGFP traces was the Vps4-mCherry signal sufficiently high for analysis.
source: Although all the Vps4-mCherry traces coincided with Snf7-eGFP or Vps24-eGFP traces (Figure 3b,c), only in about 32% of them (more than 3300 traces) was the Vps4-mCherry signal sufficiently high for subsequent analysis.
evidence: This describes a limitation due to photobleaching of mCherry

claim: The intensity fluctuations of Snf7-eGFP and of Vps24-eGFP correlated with those of Vps4-mCherry in the same trace.
source: The intensity fluctuations of Snf7-eGFP and of Vps24-eGFP correlated with those of Vps4-mCherry in the same trace (Figure 4a).
evidence: Supported by cross-correlation analysis of dual-color traces

claim: The cross-correlation of amplitude and its derivative had single peaks at the origin, indicating coordinated recruitment dynamics of Vps4 and ESCRT-III components.
source: In both cases, the cross-correlation of amplitude and its derivative had single peaks at the origin, indicating coordinated recruitment dynamics of Vps4 and the ESCRT-III components, at least on a time scale longer than the resolution of our determinations (850 ms).
evidence: Supported by cross-correlation analysis

claim: The lifetime and dynamics properties of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP were indistinguishable.
source: Though the fast photobleaching of Vps4-mCherry precluded the correlational analysis of the remaining traces, the lifetime (the interval between the appearance and disappearance of above-baseline intensity) of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP (Figure 4b,d) and dynamics properties (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplements 2–4) were indistinguishable.
evidence: Supported by statistical comparison of lifetime distributions

claim: The lifetime followed similar bi-exponential distributions for all Snf7 and Vps24 events.
source: The lifetime followed similar bi-exponential distributions for all Snf7 and Vps24 events (Figure 4b, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by fitting of lifetime distribution data

claim: The maximum amount of Snf7-eGFP in the traces had modes that ranged from 30 ± 9 during the initial 750 ms to 38 ± 12 for the longest-lived structures (10–51 s).
source: The maximum amount of Snf7-eGFP in the traces had a relatively broad distribution (Figure 4c), with modes that ranged from 30 ± 9 during the initial 750 ms to 38 ± 12 for the longest-lived structures (10–51 s) (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of maximum accumulation data

claim: These structures would contain an overall average of between 75 and 200 Snf7 subunits.
source: Thus, these structures would contain an overall average of between 75 and 200 Snf7 subunits, with very few of the structures containing 200 or more (Figure 4c,d).
evidence: This is calculated from the eGFP counts multiplied by the correction factor for unlabeled Snf7

claim: Vps24 recruitment had modes that ranged from 14 ± 3 during the initial 750 ms to 22 ± 6 for the longest-lived structures (10–51 s).
source: Vps24 recruitment had a broad range with modes that ranged from 14 ± 3 during the initial 750 ms to 22 ± 6 for the longest-lived structures (10–51 s) (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of Vps24-eGFP accumulation data

claim: The ratio of Snf7 to Vps24 ranges between three or five to one.
source: Assuming that all ESCRT-III assemblies have both subunits, the ratio of Snf7 to Vps24 ranges between three or five to one, in agreement with published biochemical data (Teis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is calculated from the measured fluorescence ratios and agrees with published data

claim: During the initial 750 ms, 20 ± 5 Vps4 molecules (~3 hexamers) arrived.
source: During the initial 750 ms, 20 ± 5 molecules (~3 hexamers) arrived (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of Vps4-eGFP recruitment kinetics

claim: About 20% of the events never accumulated more than 3 Vps4 hexamers at any one time.
source: About 20% of the events never accumulated more than 3 hexamers at any one time (Figure 4c) (although they gained and lost Vps4 stochastically throughout their lifetime); most of these events were of short duration.
evidence: Supported by analysis of maximum Vps4 accumulation distribution

claim: 80% of events acquired 4 or more Vps4 hexamers at any one time and were longer lived (≥5 s).
source: The 80% that acquired 4 or more hexamers at any one time were longer lived (≥5 s) (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of Vps4 accumulation and lifetime

claim: Non-productive events in cells expressing Vps4E233Q or lacking Pep12 only rarely accumulated more than 3 Vps4 hexamers.
source: Non-productive events in cells expressing a Vps4 mutant defective in ATP hydrolysis (E233Q) or in cells lacking Pep12 (see below) only rarely accumulated more than 3 Vps4 hexamers (Figure 4d, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by comparison of Vps4 accumulation in mutant vs wild-type cells

claim: Nearly all the cytosolic Vps4-eGFP was monomeric in yeast cells.
source: Using a spinning disc confocal microscope calibrated for single-molecule counting (Cocucci et al., 2012), we determined that nearly all the cytosolic Vps4-eGFP was monomeric in yeast cells, whether or not the cells were exposed to chemical crosslinking before lysis and adsorption of the cytosol onto a glass coverslip (Figure 4—figure supplement 10a–d).
evidence: Supported by single-molecule photobleaching analysis

claim: Vps4 hexamers form during recruitment of ESCRT-III to endosomes.
source: These observations suggest that Vps4 hexamers form during recruitment of ESCRT-III to endosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cytosolic Vps4 is monomeric but appears as hexamers on endosomes

claim: On perivacuolar MVBs, the maximum accumulations of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP had a mode 4–5 times larger than in peripheral objects.
source: On perivacuolar MVBs with persistent fluorescence we detected brighter signals of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP; the maximum accumulations had a relatively broad distribution with a mode 4–5 times larger (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a) than in the peripheral objects (Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by comparison of fluorescence intensities between peripheral and perivacuolar objects

claim: This is the behavior expected for optically unresolved clusters of perivacuolar MVBs.
source: This is the behavior expected for optically unresolved clusters of perivacuolar MVBs visualized by electron microscopy (Figure 2).
evidence: This interpretation is supported by the electron microscopy showing clusters of MVBs

claim: The short-time fluctuations in the numbers of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP molecules in perivacuolar objects corresponded to the numbers in spatially resolved peripheral events.
source: We also found that the short-time fluctuations in the numbers of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP molecules (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b) corresponded to the numbers of Snf7-eGFP, Vps24-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP molecules in the spatially resolved events detected in diffraction limited peripheral objects (Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by quantitative comparison of fluctuation magnitudes

claim: The fluctuations in perivacuolar objects presumably represented individual budding events observed by CLEM.
source: Presumably they represented individual budding events we observed by CLEM (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an inference connecting the optical and EM observations

claim: Pep12 is essential for fusion of early endocytic carriers.
source: Fusion of the early, small endocytic carriers is a prerequisite for MVB formation. Pep12 (the yeast syntaxin homolog) is essential for fusion; its absence leads to the accumulation of 40–50 nm diameter endosomes, which are too small to accommodate ILVs, and thus fail to deliver endocytic cargo into the vacuole (Becherer et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: Absence of Pep12 leads to accumulation of 40–50 nm diameter endosomes that are too small to accommodate ILVs.
source: Fusion of the early, small endocytic carriers is a prerequisite for MVB formation. Pep12 (the yeast syntaxin homolog) is essential for fusion; its absence leads to the accumulation of 40–50 nm diameter endosomes, which are too small to accommodate ILVs, and thus fail to deliver endocytic cargo into the vacuole (Becherer et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: Electron micrographs of pep12Δ cells expressing Vps4-eGFP showed eGFP-specific antibody labeling on small vesicles, ~45 ± 18 nm in diameter (n = 439) devoid of ILVs.
source: Electron micrographs of Pep12 deficient (pep12Δ) cells expressing Vps4-eGFP showed eGFP-specific antibody labeling on small vesicles, ~45 ± 18 nm in diameter (n = 439) devoid of ILVs, as expected (Figure 4—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Supported by immuno-EM data

claim: In most pep12Δ cell images, 2–3 vesicles formed small clusters.
source: In most of the images, 2–3 vesicles formed small clusters.
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy observations

claim: LLSM imaging of pep12Δ cells expressing Snf7-eGFP or Vps4-eGFP showed fluorescent puncta spatially distributed like the peripheral and perivacuolar endosomes seen in WT cells.
source: LLSM imaging of pep12Δ cells expressing Snf7-eGFP or Vps4-eGFP showed fluorescent puncta, spatially distributed like the peripheral and perivacuolar endosomes seen in WT cells (Figure 3c,e).
evidence: Supported by LLSM imaging data

claim: The lifetimes of peripheral events in pep12Δ cells were similar to those of comparable events in WT cells and cells expressing Vps4E233Q.
source: The lifetimes of the peripheral events were similar to those of comparable events in WT cells and cells expressing Vps4E233Q (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplements 5 and 6, see below).
evidence: Supported by statistical comparison of lifetime distributions

claim: The intensity distribution of Snf7-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP in pep12Δ cells had two distinct peaks.
source: The intensity distribution of Snf7-eGFP and Vps4-eGFP in pep12Δ cells had two distinct peaks (Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by analysis of fluorescence intensity distributions

claim: The distribution for Vps4-eGFP in pep12Δ cells corresponded to 2 and 4 hexamers, respectively.
source: The distribution for Vps4-eGFP corresponded to 2 and 4 hexamers, respectively (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 10f,g, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of Vps4-eGFP intensity distribution

claim: The first peak in pep12Δ cells likely represented single small endocytic carriers while the second likely represented clusters of at least two small endocytic carriers.
source: The former peak likely represented single small endocytic carriers while the latter likely represented the clusters of at least two small endocytic carriers seen in the EM images.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the optical and EM observations

claim: The dynamics of Snf7 in pep12Δ cells was similar to WT cells.
source: The dynamics of Snf7 was similar to WT cells (Figure 4d).
evidence: Supported by comparison of Snf7 recruitment dynamics

claim: The Vps4 dynamics at peripheral events in pep12Δ cells resembled those in Vps4E233Q cells more closely than those in WT cells.
source: In contrast, the Vps4 dynamics at peripheral events in pep12Δ cells (Figure 4d) resembled those in Vps4E233Q cells more closely than they did those in WT cells.
evidence: Supported by comparison of Vps4 recruitment dynamics across conditions

claim: Constitutive expression of Vps4E233Q causes disappearance of MVBs and formation of flat, cisternal membrane stacks - the 'class E compartment'.
source: Constitutive expression of Vps4E233Q, a mutant that is impaired in ATP hydrolysis, causes disappearance of MVBs and formation instead of flat, cisternal membrane stacks - the 'class E compartment' - on which ESCRT-III complexes and Vps4 accumulate (Babst et al., 1997; Babst et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: ESCRT-III complexes and Vps4 accumulate on the class E compartment.
source: Constitutive expression of Vps4E233Q, a mutant that is impaired in ATP hydrolysis, causes disappearance of MVBs and formation instead of flat, cisternal membrane stacks - the 'class E compartment' - on which ESCRT-III complexes and Vps4 accumulate (Babst et al., 1997; Babst et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: LLSM imaging of cells expressing Vps4E233Q-eGFP showed substantial entrapment of Vps4E233Q-eGFP and ESCRT-III subunits in class E compartments.
source: LLSM imaging of cells expressing Vps4E233Q-eGFP as the only Vps4 species showed a substantial entrapment of Vps4E233Q-eGFP (Figure 3e, Figure 3—figure supplement 1e, Video 5) and ESCRT-III subunits in class E compartments (Figure 3c,d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d, Videos 6 and 7).
evidence: Supported by LLSM imaging data

claim: Class E compartments are large, very bright, relatively static perivacuolar objects with lifetimes longer than the time series.
source: These large, very bright, relatively static perivacuolar objects always had lifetimes longer than the time series.
evidence: Supported by LLSM tracking data

claim: Diffraction limited, mobile, peripheral objects (about 5–10 per yeast cell) were detected in Vps4E233Q cells.
source: We also detected in these cells diffraction limited, mobile, peripheral objects (about 5–10 detected per yeast cell within the 51 s time window) (Figure 3c–e, Videos 5–7).
evidence: Supported by LLSM imaging data

claim: The distribution of lifetimes for 93% of peripheral objects in cells expressing Vps4E233Q-eGFP was almost identical to the distribution in cells expressing wild-type Vps4-eGFP.
source: The distribution of lifetimes for 93% of the peripheral objects in cells expressing Vps4E233Q-eGFP was almost identical to the distribution of similar objects in cells only expressing wild-type Vps4-eGFP (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 9, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by statistical comparison of lifetime distributions

claim: 7% of peripheral objects in Vps4E233Q cells persisted beyond the 51 s time window, suggesting impaired or slower release of Vps4E233Q-eGFP unable to hydrolyze ATP.
source: The remaining peripheral objects persisted beyond the 51 s time window suggesting impaired or slower release of Vps4E233Q-eGFP unable to hydrolyze ATP (Figure 4b, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by analysis of persistent tracks in Vps4E233Q cells

claim: Vps4 lifetimes in peripheral endosomes are independent of Vps4 ATPase activity.
source: We conclude from this unexpected result that Vps4 lifetimes in peripheral endosomes are independent of Vps4 ATPase activity and that association and release of Vps4 can occur in the absence of ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the similar lifetimes in wild-type and Vps4E233Q cells

claim: Association and release of Vps4 can occur in the absence of ATP hydrolysis.
source: We conclude from this unexpected result that Vps4 lifetimes in peripheral endosomes are independent of Vps4 ATPase activity and that association and release of Vps4 can occur in the absence of ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation of dynamic Vps4 recruitment in Vps4E233Q cells

claim: Recruitment of Snf7-eGFP or Vps24-eGFP to peripheral objects in cells expressing Vps4E233Q-mCherry had essentially the same dynamic characteristics as in cells expressing wt Vps4-mCherry.
source: Recruitment of Snf7-eGFP or of Vps24-eGFP to the peripheral objects, in cells expressing Vps4E233Q-mCherry, had essentially the same dynamic characteristics as in cells expressing wt Vps4-mCherry (Figure 4c - d, Figure 4—figure supplements 7 and 8; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by comparison of ESCRT-III recruitment dynamics

claim: Expression of Vps4E233Q-mCherry led to accumulation of Snf7-eGFP in a fraction of peripheral and all perivacuolar endosomes.
source: Expression of Vps4E233Q-mCherry led to the accumulation of Snf7-eGFP in a fraction of peripheral and all perivacuolar endosomes (Figure 4c,d, Figure 4—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: Supported by LLSM imaging data

claim: ESCRT-III assembly and release events occur on endosomes in the absence of Vps4 ATPase activity, but none result in ILV budding.
source: Thus ESCRT-III assembly and release events occurred on endosomes but absence of Vps4 ATPase activity means that none result in ILV budding.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of ESCRT-III dynamics without ILV formation in Vps4E233Q cells

claim: The intensity distribution of peripheral, diffraction limited Vps4E233Q-eGFP containing structures peaked at about 11 ± 3 molecules, about two Vps4 hexamers.
source: The intensity distribution of the peripheral, diffraction limited Vps4E233Q-eGFP containing structures peaked at about 11 ± 3 molecules, that is, about two Vps4 hexamer -- less than the maximum of 4 or more found with the wild-type protein (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 10f; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of Vps4E233Q-eGFP intensity distribution

claim: The intensity distribution for Vps4E233Q mutant was independent of the lifetime of the object, unlike wild-type Vps4-eGFP.
source: Moreover, the intensity distribution for the mutant was independent of the lifetime of the object, unlike wild-type Vps4-eGFP, for which longer traces were in general brighter (Figure 4d).
evidence: Supported by comparison of intensity vs lifetime relationships

claim: The levels of Vps4E233Q-eGFP at peripheral endosomes are similar to those of Vps4-eGFP in pep12Δ cells.
source: The levels of Vps4E233Q-eGFP at peripheral endosomes are similar to those of Vps4-eGFP in pep12Δ cells (Figure 4d).
evidence: Supported by comparison of Vps4 accumulation levels

claim: Both Vps4E233Q and pep12Δ mutations fail to support ILV formation.
source: Both mutations fail to support ILV formation - in Vps4E233Q-eGFP cells because there is no source of energy for deforming the membrane and in pep12Δ cells because the unfused carrier vesicles are too small.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why ILV formation fails in these mutants

claim: Rapamycin-induced heterodimerization of Vps4-eGFP-FRB with Pma1-FKBP12 rapidly depleted the cytoplasmic Vps4-eGFP-FRB pool.
source: Rapamycin-induced heterodimerization of fully functional Vps4-eGFP-FRB (FRB: FKBP12 rapamycin binding domain) (Figure 5a), with Pma1-FKBP12 (the abundant plasma-membrane H+-ATPase, Pma1, fused to the 12 kDa FK506 binding protein, FKBP12) rapidly depleted the cytoplasmic Vps4-eGFP-FRB pool.
evidence: Supported by live cell microscopy showing Vps4 relocalization to plasma membrane

claim: Within a minute after rapamycin addition, most of the Vps4-eGFP-FRB had anchored irreversibly to Pma1-FKBP12.
source: Within a minute after rapamycin addition, most of the Vps4-eGFP-FRB had anchored irreversibly to Pma1-FKBP12 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse microscopy after rapamycin addition

claim: Acute Vps4 depletion prevented delivery of cargo to the vacuole and caused accumulation of MVB cargo molecules in perivacuolar endosomes.
source: Live cell microscopy showed that depletion of Vps4 prevented delivery of cargo to the vacuole and caused instead an accumulation of MVB cargo molecules in perivacuolar endosomes (Figure 5a).
evidence: Supported by live cell microscopy of cargo trafficking after Vps4 depletion

claim: After acute Vps4 depletion, the number of ILVs per MVB decreased.
source: Although ESCRT-III was still recruited, the number of ILVs per MVB decreased, while the number of MVBs with ILV buds did not increase (Figure 5d).
evidence: Supported by electron tomography after rapamycin-induced Vps4 depletion

claim: After acute Vps4 depletion, the number of MVBs with ILV buds did not increase.
source: Although ESCRT-III was still recruited, the number of ILVs per MVB decreased, while the number of MVBs with ILV buds did not increase (Figure 5d).
evidence: Supported by electron tomography after rapamycin-induced Vps4 depletion

claim: After 10 min of Vps4 depletion, the number of endosomes lacking ILV buds increased.
source: In contrast, after 10 min the number of endosomes lacking ILV buds increased (Figure 5d).
evidence: Supported by electron tomography at 10 min time point

claim: ILV budding (membrane buckling) and scission stall when the cytosolic pool of Vps4 is reduced.
source: These observations suggest that ILV budding (e.g. membrane buckling) and scission stall when the cytosolic pool of Vps4 is reduced and that fusion of 'older' MVBs with the vacuole then leaves only empty, 'younger' MVBs, with incomplete buds (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the electron tomography results after Vps4 depletion

claim: Mup1-eGFP can reach the vacuole from the plasma membrane in less than 15 min after methionine addition.
source: The timing for this sequence of events is consistent with our observation that Mup1-eGFP can reach the vacuole from the plasma membrane less than 15 min after methionine addition (see also Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Video 8), and with earlier work (Arlt et al., 2015) showing that alpha-factor also trafficked within 15 min from the plasma membrane to the vacuole.
evidence: Supported by time-lapse LLSM imaging of cargo trafficking

claim: Alpha-factor trafficked within 15 min from the plasma membrane to the vacuole.
source: The timing for this sequence of events is consistent with our observation that Mup1-eGFP can reach the vacuole from the plasma membrane less than 15 min after methionine addition (see also Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Video 8), and with earlier work (Arlt et al., 2015) showing that alpha-factor also trafficked within 15 min from the plasma membrane to the vacuole.
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: At 120 min after Vps4 depletion, few endosomes with large budding structures and very few ILVs or flat cisternal membrane stacks reminiscent of class E compartments were found.
source: At the 120 min point, we found few endosomes with large budding structures and with very few ILVs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1d) or flat cisternal membrane stacks, reminiscent of class E compartments (Figure 5d).
evidence: Supported by electron tomography at 120 min time point

claim: Abrupt loss of free Vps4 stalled ILV budding and scission even though dynamic recruitment of ESCRT-III persisted.
source: Thus, abrupt loss of free Vps4 stalled ILV budding and scission even though the dynamic recruitment of ESCRT-III persisted.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the anchor-away experiments

claim: Similar results to the 120 min time point were observed under long-term conditions in cells expressing mutants of Snf7 and Vps2 unable to interact with Vps4.
source: Similar results to the 120 min time point (Figure 5—figure supplement 1d) were observed under long-term conditions in cells expressing mutants of Snf7 and Vps2 unable to interact with Vps4 including the appearance of a small number of endosomes with large budding structures mostly devoid of ILVs (Adell et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by comparison with published data on Snf7 and Vps2 mutants

claim: Several active Vps4 hexamers participate in a single budding and fission event.
source: The most straightforward molecular interpretation of our new results is that several active Vps4 hexamers participate in a single budding and fission event and that an incomplete bud will stall if no more Vps4 can add.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the acute Vps4 depletion results

claim: An incomplete bud will stall if no more Vps4 can add.
source: The most straightforward molecular interpretation of our new results is that several active Vps4 hexamers participate in a single budding and fission event and that an incomplete bud will stall if no more Vps4 can add.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the stalled buds observed after Vps4 depletion

claim: Current models for ILV formation assume gradual accumulation of ESCRT-III proteins, followed by a burst of Vps4 at the end of the process.
source: Current models for ILV formation assume gradual accumulation of ESCRT-III proteins, followed by a burst of Vps4 at the end of the process (Schöneberg et al., 2017).
evidence: This summarizes existing models in the literature

claim: Current models invoke the properties of ESCRT-III polymerization linked to a membrane surface as the driving force for membrane deformation.
source: The models invoke the properties of ESCRT-III polymerization linked to a membrane surface as the driving force for membrane deformation; free energy input from ATP hydrolysis by Vps4 then re-sets the system by recycling the ESCRT-III components.
evidence: This summarizes existing models in the literature

claim: Current models propose that ATP hydrolysis by Vps4 re-sets the system by recycling ESCRT-III components.
source: The models invoke the properties of ESCRT-III polymerization linked to a membrane surface as the driving force for membrane deformation; free energy input from ATP hydrolysis by Vps4 then re-sets the system by recycling the ESCRT-III components.
evidence: This summarizes existing models in the literature

claim: The live-cell imaging data are not consistent with the proposed sequence of events in current models.
source: Our live-cell imaging data are not consistent with this proposed sequence of events, nor are they easily reconciled with the assumption that ATP hydrolysis is needed only to complete the assembly-disassembly cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the discrepancy between the data and existing models

claim: The data are not easily reconciled with the assumption that ATP hydrolysis is needed only to complete the assembly-disassembly cycle.
source: Our live-cell imaging data are not consistent with this proposed sequence of events, nor are they easily reconciled with the assumption that ATP hydrolysis is needed only to complete the assembly-disassembly cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that Vps4 ATPase activity is required during budding, not just at the end

claim: Appearance and disappearance of Snf7 and Vps4 at peripheral endosomes correlate.
source: First, appearance and disappearance of Snf7 and Vps4 at peripheral endosomes correlate, as do appearance and disappearance of Vps24 and Vps4.
evidence: Supported by cross-correlation analysis of dual-color traces

claim: Appearance and disappearance of Vps24 and Vps4 at peripheral endosomes correlate.
source: First, appearance and disappearance of Snf7 and Vps4 at peripheral endosomes correlate, as do appearance and disappearance of Vps24 and Vps4.
evidence: Supported by cross-correlation analysis of dual-color traces

claim: Snf7 and Vps24 must co-assemble.
source: Therefore Snf7 and Vps24 must also correlate.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the correlation of both with Vps4

claim: If Vps24 and Vps2 are recruited jointly, then all three ESCRT-III components (Snf7, Vps24, Vps2) will co-assemble.
source: Moreover, if Vps24 and Vps2 are recruited jointly, as earlier evidence suggests (Teis et al., 2008; Babst et al., 2002), then all these three ESCRT-III components will co-assemble, presumably into filamentous structures related to the diverse forms seen in vitro.
evidence: This is an inference based on published evidence for joint recruitment

claim: The data from LLSM show coordinated, rather than sequential recruitment of ESCRT-III components.
source: Although Vps24 and Vps2 are sometimes called 'capping proteins', because they are required for the recruitment of Vps4 and thus restrict the growth of Snf7 filaments in vivo (Teis et al., 2008; Babst et al., 2002) and in vitro (Mierzwa et al., 2017) our data from LLSM show coordinated, rather than sequential recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cross-correlation analysis showing simultaneous recruitment

claim: The average numbers of Snf7 and Vps24 subunits present during an event are about 60 to 150 Snf7 and 14 to 30 Vps24 (20th to 80th percentile).
source: Second, during the lifetime of ESCRT-III assemblies on a peripheral endosome, which ranges from 3 s to a substantial fraction of a minute, the average numbers of Snf7 and Vps24 subunits present during the event, subject to uncertainties about the incorporation ratio of tagged and untagged Snf7, are about 60 to 150 Snf7 and 14 to 30 Vps24, respectively (representing 20th to 80th percent of the distributions, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of mean accumulation data

claim: Initial recruitment of ESCRT-III is abrupt, rather than gradually cumulative.
source: Initial recruitment is abrupt, rather than gradually cumulative.
evidence: Supported by observation of rapid rise in fluorescence at the start of traces

claim: Termination of ESCRT-III recruitment is abrupt.
source: Termination is likewise abrupt.
evidence: Supported by observation of rapid decline in fluorescence at the end of traces

claim: Both ESCRT-III components fluctuate substantially, with no evident pattern, during the lifetime of the presumptive nascent bud.
source: Both components fluctuate substantially, with no evident pattern, during the lifetime of the presumptive nascent bud.
evidence: Supported by analysis of fluorescence intensity fluctuations

claim: The fluctuations in ESCRT-III components are abrupt.
source: The fluctuations, like the initial accumulation, are abrupt; the magnitudes of these fluctuations (Supplementary file 2) can be nearly as great as the overall averages.
evidence: Supported by analysis of fluctuation dynamics

claim: The magnitudes of ESCRT-III fluctuations can be nearly as great as the overall averages.
